sources.title: Hubertus von Gall, Karafto Caves
sources.note: 2010 article, updated 2016; author participated in 1975 documentation. Carved architecture is observed; sanctuary/assembly/residential function remains debated.

sources.title: Antigoni Zournatzi, Karaftō: Greek apotropaic inscription (2016)
sources.note: National Hellenic Research Foundation catalogue, after Rougemont 2012, Corpus Inscriptionum Iranicarum II.I.1 no. 75. Second line is unbracketed; date late fourth or first half of third century BCE by letter forms.

sources.title: Strabo, Geography 11.13, translated by H. L. Jones
sources.note: Later literary portrait around the beginning of the Common Era. Sections 1 to 3 distinguish Atropatene from Greater Media. Group all Strabo Geography URLs for cumulative attribution.

sources.title: British Library, Add MS 38895 A: Greek deed of sale of a vineyard
sources.note: Catalogue gives alternative dates 88 BCE or 24 BCE, depending on era; Greek recto, Parthian verso, duplicated text with differences. Avroman lies outside the imported polygon.

sources.title: Kimberley Czajkowski, Parchments and Papyri (2022)
sources.note: A Companion to the Hellenistic and Roman Near East, pages 105 to 113; directly accessible scholarly abstract explains Avroman discovery and double-document security.

proposedOverrides.summary: An Iranian regional kingdom whose history extended well beyond this map’s 323 to 200 BCE window.

batchIdentityNotes.decision: One exact indexed record only, no aliases. Two identical polygons cover -323 to -300 and -300 to -200. The 300 seam is not a dynasty event. Separate from Greater Media, Armenia, Seleucid/Parthian empires and modern Azerbaijan.
batchIdentityNotes.geometry: Bounding box 43.3894,36.1885 to 51.4175,40.4258. Core northwestern Iran; Karafto and Avroman test outside. Public overview and example paragraphs explicitly identify both as outside-outline regional evidence.
batchIdentityNotes.limitations: No securely attributable household excavation, children’s school, hospital or toilet system from the exact map window was established in the checked sources. Do not invent these. Karafto is not proven to have been an Atropatid commission. Greek sample is regional, not a reconstructed local Iranian phrase. Avroman belongs to a later period; catalogue dating alternative retained. Historical political continuity extends beyond the atlas endpoint.
